content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to CAPM Certification in Los Alamos

steps_items.heading: Verify Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: CAPM requires a secondary degree and completion of project management education hours—but no prior work experience. If you hold a high school diploma, associate degree, or equivalent, you meet the education prerequisite. This makes CAPM ideal for professionals new to project management across Los Alamos's national security, research, and federal sectors.

steps_items.heading: Complete 23 Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led boot camp. Our intensive format covers all CAPM domains—project integration, scope, schedule, cost, quality, communications, and more—in a condensed timeline. You'll work through real-world scenarios and interactive exercises with active certified practitioners, all from your Los Alamos location.

steps_items.heading: Apply to PMI and Pay Exam Fee
steps_items.text: Submit your PMI application once you complete training. You'll provide proof of your secondary degree and education completion to verify eligibility. Pay the exam fee through PMI's portal. Our admissions team can guide you through the application process and answer eligibility questions.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Take the Exam
steps_items.text: Granite PM Academy provides exam-preparation resources, practice questions, and study guides to reinforce your learning. Schedule your computer-based CAPM exam at a testing center near Los Alamos or take it online. Our instructors are available to clarify concepts and build your confidence before test day.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: CAPM is valid for three years. During each renewal cycle, earn professional development units (PDUs) through training, certifications, and project management activities. Staying current keeps your credential active and demonstrates ongoing commitment to your professional growth in Los Alamos's competitive project-driven environment.

fq_items.question: Do I need project management experience to take the CAPM?
fq_items.answer: No prior PM experience is required. The CAPM only requires secondary education (high school diploma or equivalent) and 23 contact hours of project management education — which our course fulfills.

fq_items.question: Is the CAPM a good starting credential for {city} professionals?
fq_items.answer: Yes. The CAPM is one of the most recognized entry-level PM credentials and is highly regarded across industries in {city_state}. It demonstrates PM knowledge to employers even before you have years of experience.

fq_items.question: How does the CAPM differ from the PMP?
fq_items.answer: The PMP requires 36–60 months of project leadership experience; the CAPM does not. Many professionals earn the CAPM early in their career, gain experience, then pursue the PMP.

fq_items.question: Is this training delivered online?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Our CAPM training is fully live-virtual — no travel required. {city} students attend via video conference from wherever they are.

fq_items.question: Is CAPM certification worth pursuing for Los Alamos National Laboratory careers?

LANL and its contractor partners increasingly value CAPM as evidence of structured project management capability, especially for roles supporting federal programs requiring rigorous controls and compliance. While PMP® certification has become more prominent among senior project managers at LANL contractors, CAPM serves as a recognized entry point for professionals building credentials in national security research, nuclear science, and defense work—fields where demonstrated project discipline directly influences career advancement and compensation opportunity.

fq_items.question: Which Los Alamos employers specifically recognize CAPM certification?
fq_items.answer: LANL prime contractors—including Triad National Security, LLC, N3B Los Alamos, and similar firms managing large federal programs—recognize CAPM as a credential signaling readiness for project coordinator and junior project manager roles. The U.S. Department of Energy (Los Alamos Field Office) and NNSA-aligned organizations also value it. Environmental remediation, IT security, and scientific research contractors operating in Los Alamos similarly view CAPM as evidence of professional project management training aligned with federal and national laboratory standards.

fq_items.answer: Project managers in Los Alamos, particularly those supporting LANL contractors, see compensation influenced heavily by security clearance level, technical expertise, and program scope—factors that often outweigh certification alone.
